source: Water Quality Portal (EPA/USGS) Result search, CSV
flags: Arsenic: the Water Quality Portal returned 867 result rows within 25 miles — uninterpreted regional samples, not a parcel finding. CT DPH/USGS study: 3.9% of CT private wells exceeded the arsenic MCL. Connecticut requires arsenic testing for new wells — confirm the lab runs the state-required panel.

Uranium: the Water Quality Portal returned 2765 result rows within 25 miles — uninterpreted regional samples, not a parcel finding. CT DPH/USGS study: 4.7% of CT private wells exceeded the uranium MCL. Connecticut requires uranium testing for new wells — confirm the lab runs the state-required panel.
Radon in water: no queryable public result dataset found — ask the lab whether to include radon; common in CT bedrock.
note: Counts are regional sample rows, not parcel predictions. Connecticut requires arsenic and uranium testing for newly constructed private and semipublic wells (CT DPH, effective Oct 1, 2022) — confirm the exact panel with a certified lab.
final_word: Risk flags are not a prediction. Laboratory testing of the finished well is the final word.
